correctness.rationale: The normalized three-dimensional scaled NLP-Id determinant is positive on the entire compact two-selection hypersimplex. A direct determinant expansion gives exact elementary-symmetric coefficients. Both outer spectral concavity ranges follow from affine log-determinant concavity. The additional low range follows because e2 and e3 are concave on this slice and have nonnegative coefficients. In the excluded gap the coefficient B is negative, yielding an exact positive directional second derivative at a feasible relative-interior point; all boundaries are handled. Symmetry/Jensen gives the exact maximizer and determinant formula. The derivative numerator is a concave quadratic positive at both relevant endpoints, ensuring strict monotonicity. The Hessian has uniform curvature bounded above by -B/Dmax on the extra low interval, and compactness ensures persistence for covariance perturbations. The actual standalone checker returned VERIFY_OK on 770 rational determinant configurations plus further checks; real quantifiers are proved analytically.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 work proves ambient-cube spectral sufficient intervals and a limited equicorrelation sufficient interval, but not exact necessity/sufficiency on the cardinality-two affine slice. A detailed comparison of its Theorem 17 and Remark 16, the preceding MESP/D-Opt equivalence work, and a distinct 2026 generalized factorization bound revealed no statement implying the all-scale classification, explicit slice curvature, relaxation-value monotonicity or robust off-spectral concavity. The 1996/1999 originals were not retrieved in full; that and unindexed equivalent mathematics remain risks.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent affine-slice phase classification may exist under D-optimal-design terminology or in an unindexed paper.

value.rationale: The cardinality-two slice with three coordinates is the first natural two-dimensional feasible hypersimplex of scaled maximum-entropy sampling; the motivating publication explicitly identifies affine-slice curvature as unresolved by its ambient Hessian approach. The theorem provides an exact global concavity/nonconcavity threshold, a computable strictly improving optimal relaxation value, a Euclidean strong-concavity modulus, and convex off-spectral relaxation guarantees on an open class of non-equicorrelated matrices with nonidentical discrete selection values. It is a structural phase classification with a motivated robustness consequence, not a textbook restatement, routine enumerated invariant, or claim of global algorithm speedup.
